REQ-SAG-0601

REQ-SAG-0401 Credential resolution order and keyring defaults

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.6.0

Statements

  • `sc-agent` MUST resolve a key from the sources in the resolution order.
  • `sc-agent` MUST use the credential from the first source in the resolution order in which the credential is present.
  • The keyring service MUST be that provider's credential-variable name.
  • The keyring account MUST be the current OS account.

Requirement

Definitions: A *provider* is an endpoint that serves a model; a provider that names a credential-variable name has a key that `sc-agent` resolves, and a keyless provider (a local model) has none. A *credential* is the API key for one provider. A *credential-variable name* is the name of the environment variable that holds a provider's credential. The *keyring service* and the *keyring account* are the two components that identify a provider's entry in the platform keyring. The *resolution order* is the process environment, then the repository-root `.env` file, then the platform keyring (the OS credential store: Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, Secret Service on Linux). A credential is *present* in a source when the source holds a value under the provider's credential-variable name; a blank platform-keyring value counts as absent. The *current OS account* is the user name of the operating-system user running the process.

Rationale

Credential handling stays in one place, so redaction and key lookup cannot disagree about which variables hold secrets. Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "Keyring is super basic." Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "Isn't ENV > .env > keyring (or win/linux equivalent) standard order?" A variable already set in the environment wins over `.env`, which is also dotenvy's default. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "Keyring is super basic." Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

With a valid key in the environment, a different valid key in the repository-root `.env` and another in the keyring, the environment key is used; with none in the environment, the `.env` key is used; with neither, the keyring key is used.

REQ-SAG-0101 Model short names

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.5.0

Statements

  • Each cloud short name MUST resolve to a model in the `sc-agent` model table.
  • Each local short name MUST resolve to a local model in the model table.

Requirement

Definitions: A short name is a model name without a version. The cloud short names are `jev`, `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`, `fable`, `luna`, `terra`, `sol` and `astra`. The local short names are `laya` and `decider`. A local model is a row whose provider is an endpoint on a computer the user runs.

Rationale

sc-agent launches any model, not only decision models, and callers select models by short name. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test resolves each cloud short name to a model in the model table.
  • A unit test resolves each local short name to a local model in the model table.

Related

REQ-SAG-0102

REQ-SAG-0102 Model catalog: built-in and configured model rows

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.9.0

Statements

  • The built-in rows of the model table MUST be sorted by release date, newest first.
  • A short name MUST resolve to its newest row in the model table, unless a configured model entry for that name overrides it (REQ-SAG-0019).
  • A full model id MUST select its row exactly.
  • Each built-in model MUST carry the model's published release date.
  • `sc-agent` MUST NOT branch on a catalog name.

Requirement

Definitions: `sc-agent` is the program this record governs. The model table is the list of models built into `sc-agent`, together with the rows configuration adds. Each row has a short name, a fixed model id, a release date and a provider. A built-in model is a row built into `sc-agent`, not added by configuration. A full model id is a row's fixed model id, such as `claude-haiku-5-5`. A model's published release date is the date its maker announced the model as available. A catalog name is a provider name, a short name or a model id. To branch on a catalog name is to compare it with a string literal to choose what the code does.

Rationale

When a new model is released, short names such as `haiku`, `luna`, `opus` and `sol` must launch it immediately. Hard-coded rows go stale quickly, so configuration can add rows, and a configured row wins its short name (owner ruling 2026-11-25). When several providers serve the newest row, REQ-SAG-0103 orders them. Provider and model are values carried in typed data, not names to branch on. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test verifies that, with a configuration row added, the built-in rows are sorted by release date, newest first, and the configuration row is selected for its short name.
  • A unit test verifies that, of two rows sharing a short name, the short name resolves to the row with the later release date.
  • A unit test verifies that selecting a built-in row's full model id returns that row.
  • A unit test verifies that every built-in row has a release date.
  • A search of `crates/sc-agent/src` finds no comparison of a catalog name with a string literal outside the model and provider tables.

Related

  • REQ-SAG-0101
  • REQ-SAG-0103

REQ-SAG-0103 Provider and model are separate

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.5.0

Statements

  • A model-table row MUST store its provider in a field separate from its model.
  • A request MUST carry the model id stored in the selected model-table row.
  • sc-agent MUST be able to send requests through Together.
  • sc-agent MUST be able to send requests through OpenRouter.
  • When configuration names a provider for a model, sc-agent MUST send that model's requests to that provider.
  • When no provider is configured for a model, sc-agent MUST prefer a provider that needs no key over one that needs a key.
  • When no provider is configured for a model and every provider serving it needs a key, sc-agent MUST use the first of them whose key is found.
  • The provider that sends requests to the OpenAI API MUST have the name `openai`.
  • A short name MUST NOT encode its provider.
  • A request MUST NOT require the caller to name a provider.

Requirement

Definitions: sc-agent is this project's client library and command-line tool that sends model requests. A provider is the service a request is sent to, such as OpenRouter, Nous, Together, OpenAI or Anthropic. A model is what that provider runs. A model id is the name a provider uses for a model, such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` at OpenRouter. A short name is the name a caller uses for a model, such as `haiku`. The model table is the list of models sc-agent can send to, one row per model and provider (REQ-SAG-0102). A key is the secret credential a provider requires before it accepts a request; a keyless provider requires none. The OpenAI API is the request service run by OpenAI.

Rationale

The owner uses OpenRouter, Nous, Together, OpenAI and Anthropic today, and one model can be served by more than one provider. Making the caller pick a provider per call is poor UX and unreliable over time. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • Unit test: every model-table row stores its provider in a field separate from its model.
  • Unit test: a short name served by two providers is the same string for both rows.
  • Unit test: the short name `haiku` selects the same model through two different providers, and each sends its own id: `claude-haiku-5-5` through `anthropic` and `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` through `openrouter`.
  • Unit test: with `openrouter` configured for `haiku` and the `anthropic` key also found, a `haiku` request goes to `openrouter`.
  • Unit test: with no provider configured, a model served by a keyless provider and a keyed provider goes to the keyless one.
  • Unit test: with no provider configured and only the `openrouter` key found, a `haiku` request goes to `openrouter`.
  • Unit test: requests can be sent through `together` and through `openrouter`.
  • Unit test: a request that names only a model, with no provider, is sent.
  • Unit test: the provider that sends to the OpenAI API is named `openai`.

REQ-SAG-0901 LLM decision backends return the Jev schema

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.0

Statements

  • In decider mode, the covered model answering the request MUST itself generate the `probabilities` value when the required schema includes that field.
  • In decider mode, the covered model answering the request MUST itself generate the `confidence` value when the required schema includes that field.
  • In decider mode, answers from each covered model MUST conform to the required schema.
  • Each decision request MUST specify the required schema through the provider's structured-output feature.
  • If a provider response fails to match the required schema, the decision backend MUST return `decision.schema_mismatch`.
  • The covered model handling the decision request MUST pass the request's inputs to the provider.
  • If the provider rejects a request input, the decision backend MUST return the provider's error.

Requirement

Definitions: Decider mode uses a large language model, such as Haiku or Luna, to answer a decision request in place of a decision model. The covered models are Haiku and Luna. The provider is the service to which the decision request is sent. The required schema is the Jev decision API's answer schema for the requested question type, including `probabilities` and `confidence` where Jev returns them. The provider's structured-output feature lets a request specify the schema the provider's answer must follow. A `decision.schema_mismatch` error identifies what in the provider response failed to match the required schema.

Rationale

Callers compare Jev and LLM answers directly, so every backend must return the same answer shape. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A Haiku or Luna answer to a choice, score, noul and box question parses as the Jev answer type for that question.
  • A test provider that returns a response missing `probabilities` yields `decision.schema_mismatch`.

Related

  • ADR-SAG-0001
  • REQ-SAG-0201

REQ-SAG-0801 Local decision runners come from configuration

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.7.0

Statements

  • Each local decision runner's network address MUST come from configuration.
  • Each local decision runner's model MUST have a fixed model id in the model table.
  • A selection of `decider` MUST resolve to the 4b decider model.
  • Each local decision runner MUST be selectable by its name wherever a decision model is selected.
  • Configuration MUST be able to add a local model that runs on another computer.
  • `sc-agent` MUST NOT hard-code the network address of any local decision runner.

Requirement

Definitions: The Jev API is the request and reply format of TypeSafe's Jev decision service (ADR-SAG-0001). A local decision runner is a daemon on the user's machine or network that serves a decision model through the Jev API. sc-agent has two, `laya` and `decider`. A runner's network address is its host and port. A decision model is a model that `sc-agent` can send a decision request to. The 4b decider model is the `decider-4b-v2.1` row. A local model is a model-table row whose model is served by a local decision runner. A paid API is a provider that needs an API key; its key is sent only to the provider's built-in endpoint.

Rationale

People are building local runners that duplicate the Jev API, and they differ only in where they run and how they report their loaded models. decider is an alternative local model to laya with a different connection string. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test sets `laya.host` and `laya.port` in configuration and checks the request goes to them with no rebuild.
  • A unit test finds a fixed model id in the model-table row of every local decision runner model.
  • A unit test resolves `decider` to the 4b decider row.
  • A CLI run of each command that selects a decision model accepts `--model laya` and `--model decider`.
  • A unit test with a stub local runner checks that the request it receives is in the Jev API format.
  • A unit test sends to a local model row added in configuration with another computer's host and checks the request reaches that host.
  • A search of the whole workspace, outside tests, finds no host or port literal for a local runner.
  • A unit test with configuration naming another endpoint for a paid provider checks that the provider's key is still sent only to its built-in endpoint.

Related

  • ADR-SAG-0001
  • REQ-SAG-0201

REQ-SAG-0701 Batches of decision requests run in parallel

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Statements

  • `sc-agent`'s `send_batch` MUST run the requests of one batch in parallel across workers.
  • The number of workers MUST be the `workers` setting.
  • When `workers` is not set, the number of workers MUST be 8.
  • Each result MUST carry the session ULID of the request it answers.
  • Each result MUST carry the input position of the request it answers.
  • A failed request MUST be returned as that request's error result.
  • When one request fails, the other requests of the batch MUST still run.
  • Cancelling the batch MUST stop every request that has not finished.

Requirement

Definitions: A batch is the decision requests a caller passes in one call: one JSONL file, one stdin stream or one Python call. A worker sends one request at a time. A session ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier) is the `session_id` of the session row that records a request's result. Results may be returned in any order. `send_batch` is the sc-agent function that takes a batch and returns one result per request. A session row is the record sc-agent stores for each answered request. A request's input position is its zero-based index in the batch. An error result is a result that carries the request's error in place of an answer. A cache hit is a request whose successful result is served from an existing session row (REQ-SAG-0703).

Rationale

Tasks send tens of thousands of decisions, and one slow or failed request must not hold up or stop the others. Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "I do not require results in request order." Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • With the default of 8 workers, a batch of 40 requests sent to a test server that holds every reply until 8 requests are in flight completes, and the server never sees more than 8 requests in flight.
  • Unit test: with the number of workers set to 1 in configuration, the test server never sees more than one request in flight from the same batch.
  • In a batch of 3 requests, each result carries the input position (0, 1 or 2) of the request it answers.
  • A batch in which one request fails returns that error tagged with its session ULID and returns every other result.
  • Cancelling a running batch returns cancelled results for every unfinished request.
  • A batch request that is a cache hit returns the `session_id` of the row that already holds its result.

Related

  • ADR-SAG-0001
  • REQ-SAG-0601
  • NFR-SAG-0001

REQ-SAG-0201 Jev API types live in sc-agent

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.1

Statements

  • `sc-agent` MUST define every type that maps to the Jev API.
  • `sc-agent` MUST cover 100% of the Jev API request and response.

Requirement

Definitions: The Jev API is the TypeSafe decision API (`POST /v1/systemone`, `GET /v1/models`) with the `choice`, `score`, `noul` and `box` question and answer types. A type maps to the Jev API when it represents part of a Jev API request or response.

Rationale

The first requirement for sc-agent is to expose the TypeSafe API, so any Jev query can be run through it. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • Unit tests verify that each request and response example in the TypeSafe API documentation (https://docs.typesafe.ai, OpenAPI 0.2.0 at https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json), for all four question types, round-trips through `sc-agent` without loss.
  • No crate other than `sc-agent` defines a type that maps to a Jev API field.

Related

ADR-SAG-0001

REQ-SAG-0202 Question digest computed by sc-sha

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.0

Statements

  • When sc-agent sends a question to a decision model, sc-agent MUST compute the question digest of that question.
  • sc-agent MUST record each question digest with the decision model's response to the question the digest was computed from.

Requirement

Definitions: The information is everything sent to the decision model with a question, other than the questions themselves. A single question is one question of the request. The question digest is the SHA-256 digest of the information plus one single question. The result cache is specified by REQ-SAG-0703. Its key is the hash of the full request text and the requested model, not the question digest.

Rationale

Recording the digest with the response lets a response be retrieved from the exact information and question that produced it.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test shows two sends of the same information and the same single question record the same question digest.
  • A unit test shows that changing any part of the information, or the question, changes the question digest.
  • A unit test shows a request with three questions records three question digests, one per question.

Related

REQ-SAG-0004

REQ-SAG-0502 sc-agent can launch any LLM

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.1

Statements

sc-agent MUST be able to send a request to any LLM a configured provider serves, not only decision models.

Requirement

Definitions: LLM means large language model. A provider is the service a request is sent to, such as OpenRouter, Nous, Together, OpenAI or Anthropic. A decision model is a model used for decision requests, such as Jev. sc-agent is the product provided by this repository.

Rationale

Decision models are a small part of what sc-agent does.

Acceptance criteria

A unit test verifies that sc-agent sends a request to a non-decision LLM selected by short name and returns its response.

Related

  • REQ-SAG-0101
  • REQ-SAG-0103

REQ-SAG-0301 sc-treesitter holds no agent code

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.0

Statements

  • `sc-treesitter` MUST NOT depend on any sc-agent crate other than `sc-agent`, whose error and logging it shares.
  • `sc-treesitter` MUST NOT contain agent or decision-model code.

Rationale

Source parsing is useful on its own and must not change when the agent crates change. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

`cargo tree -p sc-treesitter` lists no sc-agent crate other than `sc-agent`.

REQ-SAG-0302 Any tree-sitter grammar

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.1

Statements

  • `sc-treesitter` MUST load tree-sitter grammars.
  • `sc-treesitter` MUST run queries against any loaded grammar.
  • The first release MUST support the Python grammar.
  • The first release MUST support the Rust grammar.

Requirement

Definitions: A language id is the name a caller uses to select a grammar. A tree-sitter grammar describes a language for parsing. The query API is the `sc-treesitter` interface for running tree-sitter queries against a loaded grammar. API means application programming interface.

Rationale

The design must support any language; Python and Rust are needed first, C# and Go next.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test verifies that a query runs against Python source and against Rust source through the same API call.
  • A unit test verifies that after the second release the same call runs a query against C# source selected as `csharp` and against Go source.
  • A unit test verifies that a grammar added after release is queried through the existing API with no API change.

REQ-SAG-0303 PyO3 and CLI query surfaces

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.1

Statements

  • The `sc-treesitter` Python bindings MUST accept any tree-sitter query for any loaded tree-sitter grammar.
  • The `sitr` CLI MUST provide the `languages` subcommand.
  • The `sitr` CLI MUST provide the `queries` subcommand.
  • The `sitr` CLI MUST provide a `--version` flag.

Requirement

Definitions: CLI means command-line interface. A loaded grammar is a tree-sitter grammar loaded by `sc-treesitter`. The PyO3 bindings expose the Python query interface to `sc-treesitter`. The `sitr` CLI can expose a subset of the PyO3 query surface.

Rationale

Python callers need full query access; the CLI runs specific predefined queries that simplify common use. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: every CLI has `--version`. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A query written by the caller runs through the PyO3 bindings and returns its matches.
  • `languages` lists the loaded grammars and `queries` lists the predefined queries.
  • `sitr --version` prints the version.

ADR-SAG-0001 Every decision provider receives one request form

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.6.0

Context

sc-agent sends decisions to Jev, to local runners that serve the Jev API, and to LLM backends such as Haiku and Luna.

Problem

Jev, local Jev-compatible runners, Haiku and Luna must answer the same decision so their answers can be compared, without shared crates knowing how any one backend adapts it.

Decision

For decision requests, every decision provider receives the same Jev API request body. `sc-agent` holds one provider table and one model table; the model table is its built-in rows plus the rows configuration adds (REQ-SAG-0102), so a new model works without a release. Decision providers implement one decision trait, and LLM providers one LLM trait (JSON in, JSON out). Jev implements the decision trait over SystemOne. One type per wire format, OpenAI-compatible chat/completions and Anthropic-compatible Messages, implements both traits and is shared by every provider of that format. Before a send, the decision implementation adapts the request to its wire format; the reply is decoded back into a Jev API response. Callers open one `Run` per command (created, used for its calls, then disposed) and use its two methods, `send` for one request and `send_batch` for many; the worker threads, holdoff, cancellation and session logging live behind them.

Key principles

  • There is one decision request form: the Jev API request body.
  • `send_batch` returns each result as it is ready, tagged with its session ULID and input position; a failed request is returned in its result and the batch continues.

Rationale

When every backend receives the same data, their answers are comparable by construction, and shared code stays free of provider-specific types. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "I do not require results in request order."

Positive consequences

A new provider is added as a table row, with no change to shared types.

ADR-SAG-0002 Session logs are JSONL first, then SQLite with server sync

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.3.0

Context

The owner builds tools that read session logs to tune consumer code, analysing 10,000 to 20,000 or more decisions at a time. One task produced 40,000 sessions, each a single Jev query with its own ULID and question digest.

Problem

Session logs must be separable by repository, type of work and project, kept indefinitely, and storable long term on a server.

Decision

For the MVP, session logs are JSONL under `<log_root>/sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/` (ADR-SAG-0021). Later they load into a local SQLite database that syncs to a server for long-term storage. Every row carries its own `session_id`, `repo`, `project` and `agent_role`. All sessions of one repo, agent role and project are appended to one file in that directory; a project lasts under a day to several days.

Key principles

  • Every row describes itself, so it stays meaningful when moved or loaded.
  • Session logs are never rotated or deleted.

Rationale

JSONL is simple to write and to read with the owner's tools now. Self-describing rows load into SQLite without parsing paths, and SQLite gives indexed retrieval of a response by its question digest.

Positive consequences

Path globs select a repository, role or project without opening files.

Negative consequences

Until the SQLite stage, retrieving a response by digest needs a load of the JSONL rows.

ADR-SAG-0003 Requirements and decisions are Raptor records

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.1

Context

Requirements, non-functional requirements and architecture decisions are read by agents and by Raptor. The problem is that free-form records cannot be reliably imported into Raptor for tools to query and judge.

Decision

Every REQ, NFR and ADR is one Markdown file written from the Raptor authoring templates (`req-new.md.j2`, `nfr-new.md.j2`, `adr-new.md.j2` in randlee/raptor). Repository-wide records are under `docs/requirements/`, `docs/nfr/` and `docs/adr/`; crate-specific records are under the same folders inside `docs/<crate>/`. Changes to any record are made only in plan review and approved by the owner.

Rationale

Records that import into Raptor with no diagnostics can be queried and judged by tools, and owner approval in plan review keeps every change deliberate.

Positive consequences

Every record imports into Raptor and can be queried.

Negative consequences

Records are edited through templates, not by hand.

ADR-SAG-0004 Crate layering and error values

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Context

sc-agent will launch decision models, LLMs, CLI agents and SDK agents. Each needs shared types, configuration, secrets, HTTP and logging, but not each other's code.

Problem

Crates must be layered so each launcher depends only on what it uses, and errors must keep every lower-layer id and message.

Decision

There are five crates. `sc-agent` is the bottom layer: the provider tables, `send` and `send_batch`, resends, keys, configuration, errors, logging paths and session rows. `sc-treesitter` (tree-sitter extraction) is over `sc-agent`. On top: `decidr` (the decision CLI), `sitr` (the tree-sitter CLI) and `sc-agent-py` (the one wheel, holding the decidr and sitr APIs). CLI agents and SDK agents get their own crates later. Errors are discriminated unions: every call returns `Result<T, E>`, and `E` carries the error info: at least an id and a message. A layer that changes an error keeps the lower error's id and message (REQ-SAG-0002). An error may carry more fields. Whether a crate has its own error type or shares one is not specified.

Key principles

  • A crate depends only on lower layers.
  • The provider is chosen in one place, `sc-agent`.

Rationale

One core crate keeps the code small: ureq, keyring, dotenvy and sc-observability are called directly, with no traits or wrappers between them. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "Errors are discriminated unions Result<t,e> I don't care about per crate"; "Extra fields are fine, make sure adr doesn't limit too much. I don't want findings for returning more." Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "always return descriminated unions w/ error info"

Positive consequences

A new launcher reuses `sc-agent` without touching the other launchers.

Negative consequences

A program that wants only HTTP or logging still links the whole core.

ADR-SAG-0005 sitr's Python API is built into the sc-decidr wheel; sitr is its own crate

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Context

sc-treesitter is the tree-sitter library with two query surfaces: the Python API and the `sitr` CLI.

Problem

The Python bindings and the CLI need PyO3 and clap, but a Rust caller of the library needs neither.

Decision

`sc-agent-py`, the crate that builds the sc-decidr wheel, depends on `sc-treesitter` and exposes the sitr Python API as `sc_agent.sitr`; there is no `sc-treesitter-py` crate (ADR-SAG-0021). There is no separate sitr wheel in phase h; a standalone sitr wheel may return after the MVP, and a process uses either it or the sc-decidr wheel, never both. The `sitr` binary is its own crate, `sitr`, over `sc-treesitter`. `sc-treesitter` has no PyO3 and no clap.

Key principles

  • `sc-treesitter` pulls in no PyO3 or clap.
  • The one Python extension module is built from `sc-agent-py`, not from `sc-treesitter`.

Rationale

Keeping PyO3 in `sc-agent-py` and clap in `sitr` keeps the library's dependency set small; building the sitr API into the sc-decidr wheel gives a Python process one copy of sc-observability and one Logger for decidr and sitr calls (ADR-SAG-0021). Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Positive consequences

A Rust caller of `sc-treesitter` compiles no Python or CLI dependencies.

Negative consequences

Installing the wheel always installs both the decidr and sitr APIs.

ADR-SAG-0017 First release surfaces

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Context

Phase A ships libraries, the **decidr** decision CLI, the **sitr** tree-sitter CLI, and one Python wheel. Release must use one manifest-driven kit across five consumer channels. The problem is that every channel must release from the same tag, and per-channel workflow literals for crate lists or binary names would let the channels list different crates or binaries.

Decision

Phase A first release surfaces are **crates.io** (the crates listed in `release/publish-artifacts.toml`), **PyPI** (the `sc-decidr` wheel, holding the decidr and sitr APIs), **Homebrew**, **Scoop**, and **WinGet** (archives containing **decidr** and **sitr**), plus GitHub Release assets from the same tag. Sprints **a-11** (kit install) and **a-12** (dry-run) close the publish requirements; production uploads wait for owner dispatch.

Key principles

  • Customer-facing CLI names on channels are **decidr** and **sitr**.
  • The PyPI distribution name is **sc-decidr**.
  • No ad-hoc per-channel workflow literals for crate lists or binary names.

Rationale

- One manifest-driven kit drives all five consumer channels from the same tag. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Positive consequences

One tag drives every channel from `release/publish-artifacts.toml`.

Negative consequences

Workspace `Cargo.toml` must list members literally for kit validation.

ADR-SAG-0018 sc-publish kit owns release surface

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.1

Context

Release workflows, channel contracts, and `publish-artifacts.toml` are rendered from consumer input by [sc-publish](https://github.com/randlee/sc-publish). The problem is keeping the rendered release files consistent with that input and the pinned kit.

Decision

Edit `release/sc-publish-consumer-input.json` and re-run `install.py` from the pinned kit; do not hand-edit rendered files under `release/` or kit-owned `.github/workflows` publish YAML except through the installer.

Key principles

  • Pin a single qualified 40-character kit SHA in `release/sc-publish-pin.toml`.
  • Consumer input is the sole source of crate order, binaries, channels, and optional **docli** preflight checks.

Rationale

- The pinned kit renders release workflows and channel contracts from consumer input.

Positive consequences

Kit upgrades flow through pin bump + dry-run.

Negative consequences

Drift between JSON and rendered TOML is a hard fail until re-install.

ADR-SAG-0019 sc-decidr is the one Python decision harness

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 2.0.0

Context

sc-decidr is the harness through which sc-agent's Python consumers reach decision models (Jev, decider, Laya, Haiku, Luna). The owner requires judge-jev, plan-anchor and every later consumer to integrate identically for errors, API keys, model selection, the injectable general logger and session logging, differing only in prompt authoring and result handling. The two existing consumers each rebuilt the wheel boundary, and the copies diverged: judge-jev pins an id list with a `JEV.UNMAPPED` fallback while plan-anchor matches message text (`"http 401"`); plan-anchor pins `provider="typesafe"`, disabling Haiku and Luna; both re-sort `send_batch` results; judge-jev refuses `--timeout` while plan-anchor calls the unreleased `timeout_secs`. Consumers had no category to branch on and no per-call worker count or timeout.

Decision

The wheel is the one consumer boundary. Decision numbers are stable; there is no decision 3. 1. **The wheel is the consumer boundary.** Every consumer concern except prompt authoring and result interpretation belongs in sc-decidr: model selection, API keys (environment, repo-root `.env`, OS keyring), session logging, the general Logger, errors with a stored category (decisions 2, 5 and 6), limits and cancellation (decisions 7 and 14) and position-tagged batch results (decision 8). Session logging is always on: one row per query whose model call succeeded (a failed call writes no row; its error goes to the general log), at the wheel's default location, tagged with `project` and `agent_role`, written by sc-agent's session sink (ADR-SAG-0021); a cache hit writes no row and one link record (REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0703). All Jev queries and responses therefore take one path. **The integration artifact is a generated module** (REQ-SAG-0018), rendered by each consumer from the sc-compose template `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`; the wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout and `import sc_agent` is unchanged. - The template covers the decision call, model pass-through, logging wiring, cancellation and the error-to-category-to-code mapping. - model selectors are Run arguments. - A result line holds only the generic result fields; session data stays in the session row. The module reads session rows only through `sc_agent.session_rows`, finding a run's queries through its link records or the session_ids in its result lines, and never computes a session-log path. - Python results are typed values, not dicts. - sc-compose is an external render tool, not a wheel dependency; the template's front matter declares its sc-compose minimum (`requires.cli`), declared, not enforced. **The lower-level API stays the contract.** `Run` (with `send` and `send_batch`), `session_rows`, `provider_keys`, `TYPESAFE`, `digest`, `logger`, `log`, `flush` and `sc_agent.sitr` are public, and the generated code uses only them and the standard library. 2. **Typed fields: `attempts` and `category`.** An error value carries at least `id`, `message` and `action`, plus `attempts` (sends made, the first included) and `category` (decision 6) when they apply; unset fields are not written (REQ-SAG-0016). Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601). 5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016). 6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop. 7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. The timeout defaults to 120 s; REQ-SAG-0702 holds the rules. 8. **`send_batch` returns one result per request, each with its input position**, while `on_result` still receives each line as it finishes (REQ-SAG-0702). 11. **sitr is an optional, separate section of the consumer template.** It uses `sc_agent.sitr` only (ADR-SAG-0005, ADR-SAG-0021) and is kept separate from the decision call: extraction runs outside the decision path, and its output feeds the consumer's prompt authoring. In this phase one offline test shows extraction output reaching a dry-run request. 14. **A run is a context object.** `sc_agent.Run(tool=, tool_version=, cache=, ...)` is created once per tool command and closed when its calls are done (`with sc_agent.Run(...) as run:`); creating it mints the run's ULID `run_id` in Rust (as are `session_id` ULIDs), readable as `run.run_id`.

Rationale

Two consumers rebuilt the boundary and diverged, so the boundary moves into the wheel and integration code is generated from one template. A stored category and the send count replace message parsing and pinned id lists, and per-run limits and position-tagged results remove consumer workarounds.

Positive consequences

  • Every Python consumer renders the same integration module and holds only its prompts and result handling.
  • No consumer parses error text or pins id lists, and all Jev data takes one session-log path.

Negative consequences

The wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout.

ADR-SAG-0020 Configuration has a shared scope and one scope per CLI, each global and per worktree

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.6.0

Context

sc-agent ships two CLIs today, `decidr` and `sitr`. CLI launchers for other agent harnesses, such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Hermes and pi-agent, will be added as their peers. Apps such as plan-anchor and judge-jev wrap a CLI the way a named agent (`.claude/agents/<agent>.md`) wraps a harness. Agent-level settings, for agents such as `lai`, `sai`, `sanity`, `plan-anchor` and `judge-jev`, will later be provided by the CLI launchers. Before this decision, every CLI read one shared file pair, `~/.sc-agent/default.json` and `~/.sc-agent/local.json`, with `SC_AGENT__<KEY>` environment overrides. That layout has no per-CLI settings and no per-repository layer: two worktrees of one repository cannot hold different settings, and a setting meant for one CLI applies to all of them.

Problem

Each CLI needs its own settings, shared defaults may be overridden by a CLI file, and a repository or worktree must be able to override both.

Decision

Configuration has two kinds of scope and two locations. - The shared scope is the file `sc-agent.json`. It holds shared defaults for configuration-reading CLIs: the project/phase (ADR-SAG-0021), worker count, and optional local-runner settings. A CLI file may override those defaults. - Each CLI that reads configuration has its own scope, the file `<cli>.json` named after the CLI: `decidr.json`, and the same pattern for every CLI added later. `sitr` reads no configuration. - The global location is `~/.sc-agent/`, the user's home directory joined with `.sc-agent` on every platform, or the folder named by nonempty `SC_AGENT_HOME`. An explicit configuration directory takes precedence. - The local location is `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/`, where `<worktree>` is the root of the git work tree the CLI runs in. It holds the same file names with the same keys. The CLIs and the files each one reads are these: | CLI | Global files | Local files | Environment prefix | |---|---|---|---| | `decidr` | `~/.sc-agent/decidr.local.json`, `~/.sc-agent/decidr.json`, `~/.sc-agent/sc-agent.json` | `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.local.json`, `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.json`, `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/sc-agent.json` | `DECIDR_`, plus `SC_PROJECT` | | `sitr` | none | none | none | Every CLI has a row, and every cell is filled; a CLI that reads no file of a kind says `none`. The table is updated when a CLI is added. A setting is looked up in nine layers, and the first layer that sets it wins: 1. the CLI flag; 2. the environment variable; 3. the local `<cli>.local.json`; 4. the local `<cli>.json`; 5. the local `sc-agent.json`; 6. the global `<cli>.local.json`; 7. the global `<cli>.json`; 8. the global `sc-agent.json`; 9. the built-in default. Model entries, `models.<alias>`, are set only in configuration files, layers 3 to 8: each is a structured row (`provider` and `id` strings, `released` a `YYYY-MM-DD` date) that a flag or flat environment variable cannot express. `<alias>` becomes the row's short name. A row's provider is one sc-agent already has. Environment variables are named after the CLI: `DECIDR_<SETTING>`, with the parts of a nested key joined by a double underscore (`DECIDR_LAYA__PORT`). A setting with a wider audience than sc-agent may have its own name; the project/phase is `SC_PROJECT` (ADR-SAG-0021). Configuration files are JSON. TOML will be added when sc-config supports it (randlee/sc-runtime#152).

Key principles

  • A narrower location beats a wider one: local beats global.
  • Within one location, a CLI's own file beats the shared file.
  • sc ecosystem files in a repository live under `.sc/`, so a repository needs one `.gitignore` entry rather than one per tool.

Rationale

One file per CLI keeps each CLI's settings separate and lets a new CLI be added without touching another CLI's file. The shared file gives one place for shared defaults that a CLI file may override. The local location under `.sc/` lets each worktree differ, which matters because worktrees of one repository often work on different phases at the same time. Env vars named after the CLI keep one CLI's override from reaching another. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Positive consequences

  • A CLI added later gets its own global and local file without a schema change to any other file.
  • A worktree can override any setting without editing the user's global files.

Negative consequences

A setting can now come from nine places; `decidr doctor` reports a `path | value | source` table.

ADR-SAG-0021 One sc-observability Logger per process, owned by the entry point; general logs and session logs in separate trees

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.9.0

Context

sc-agent logs through sc-observability. The `decidr` CLI, the `sitr` CLI and the sc-decidr wheel already link the sc-observability crate. Two kinds of log exist: the general log (diagnostics, searched for issues) and session logs (the long-term record of every successful model query and its response, analysed later and loaded into SQLite, ADR-SAG-0002).

Problem

Every general-log record of a process must reach one Logger that the process's entry point owns, and every log must land at a fixed, known path, with session logs never mixed with general logs.

Decision

**One Logger per process, owned by the entry point.** The entry point is the CLI's `main`, or, for a Python app, its sc-compose generated client. The entry point obtains one sc-observability `Logger`, keeps it for the life of the process and gives it to each Run it creates (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14); the Run passes it to every decision call, flushes it after each call and on exit, and never shuts down a Logger it borrowed. The generated client has no close operation. Library code never builds a Logger of its own while one is injected, and never forwards records to Python `logging`. **The wheel exposes the crate's Logger.** Python may write its own records to it and gives it to the Run of its sc-decidr calls; Rust receives its own Logger object back, so no record crosses a bridge and the process has one queue. **Products.** sc-agent ships three products. sc-observability is a crate linked into each, not a product. | Product | Contains | |---|---| | `decidr` CLI | decidr, sc-observability | | `sitr` CLI | sitr, sc-observability | | sc-decidr wheel | the decidr and sitr Python APIs, sc-observability | There is one Python wheel. A Python process that loads sc-agent has one copy of sc-observability and one Logger, which it injects into decidr and sitr calls alike. Installing the wheel always installs both APIs, whichever one the caller uses. **Defaults.** With no Logger injected, sc-agent uses the default sc-observability Logger, which writes the general log to disk at the paths below. Every decision and sitr call is logged. A caller that wants another general-log sink (a database, nothing) changes the sink of the Logger it injects; that is the caller's responsibility. **Session log.** The session log is always on and is not configurable. sc-agent writes every session row in Rust through its session sink. No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record. A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session. Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink. **Paths.** The log root is `~/.sc-agent`. One function returns a CLI's log root. The CLIs and the wheel call that function; nothing else computes a log path. The wheel's `sc_agent.session_rows(session_ids, *, agent_role, project=None)` is the one reader of the session-log layout: it finds the log root with the same function used to write session rows and returns, as an ok value, a map from each requested `session_id` to its row; a missing id returns `session.not_found` (category `validation`) naming the ids. A generated client reads session rows only through it and has no log-root argument (NFR-SAG-0004). | Entry point | General log | Session logs | |---|---|---| | `decidr` CLI | `logs/decidr.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `sitr` CLI | `logs/sitr.log.jsonl` | none | | `plan-anchor` (generated client) | `logs/plan-anchor.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/plan-anchor/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `judge-jev` (generated client) | `logs/judge-jev.log.jsonl`, holding its decidr and sitr records | `sessions/<repo>/judge-jev/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | A wheel is not an entry point and has no row: it writes to the Logger its caller injects. Every entry point has a row and every cell is filled. The table is updated when an entry point is added. **Session identity.** - `agent_role` is the agent or app making the request. A generated client hardcodes it to its product name; it is not a user setting. - `tool` and `tool_version` name the program that sent the query and its version: the generated client's name, or `decidr` (REQ-SAG-0004). They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14). - `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files). It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set. Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase". **Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms. It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging. A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it. A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.

Key principles

  • One process, one general Logger, one queue, owned by the entry point; session rows and link records go through sc-agent's session sink, never the general Logger.
  • Session logs and general logs are never written to the same folder tree.
  • A session is never filed under a guessed project/phase.

Rationale

The entry point is the only code that knows the process's lifetime, so it is the only correct owner of the Logger: it obtains the Logger before the first general-log record and flushes after each call. Exposing the crate's own Logger from the wheel keeps one copy and one queue in the process and needs no Python package. Fixed paths keep every log in one known place for audit, and a separate `sessions/` tree lets tools and the later SQLite load read every session with a path glob. The session log is the record of every successful Jev query from every tool, so it cannot be turned off and is never rotated; it stays small enough because `project` changes over time.

Positive consequences

  • Libraries hold no logging policy: they take a Logger or use the default.
  • `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/` selects one agent's work in one phase with a path glob.

Negative consequences

Every caller must supply a project/phase before its first request.

ADR-SAG-0019 “The wheel is the one consumer boundary. Decision numbers are stable; there is no decision 3. 1. **The wheel is the consumer boundary.** Every consumer concern except prompt authoring and result interpretation belongs in sc-decidr: model selection, API keys (environment, repo-root `.env`, OS keyring), session logging, the general Logger, errors with a stored category (decisions 2, 5 and 6), limits and cancellation (decisions 7 and 14) and position-tagged batch results (decision 8). Session logging is always on: one row per query whose model call succeeded (a failed call writes no row; its error goes to the general log), at the wheel's default location, tagged with `project` and `agent_role`, written by sc-agent's session sink (ADR-SAG-0021); a cache hit writes no row and one link record (REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0703). All Jev queries and responses therefore take one path. **The integration artifact is a generated module** (REQ-SAG-0018), rendered by each consumer from the sc-compose template `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`; the wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout and `import sc_agent` is unchanged. - The template covers the decision call, model pass-through, logging wiring, cancellation and the error-to-category-to-code mapping. - model selectors are Run arguments. - A result line holds only the generic result fields; session data stays in the session row. The module reads session rows only through `sc_agent.session_rows`, finding a run's queries through its link records or the session_ids in its result lines, and never computes a session-log path. - Python results are typed values, not dicts. - sc-compose is an external render tool, not a wheel dependency; the template's front matter declares its sc-compose minimum (`requires.cli`), declared, not enforced. **The lower-level API stays the contract.** `Run` (with `send` and `send_batch`), `session_rows`, `provider_keys`, `TYPESAFE`, `digest`, `logger`, `log`, `flush` and `sc_agent.sitr` are public, and the generated code uses only them and the standard library. 2. **Typed fields: `attempts` and `category`.** An error value carries at least `id`, `message` and `action`, plus `attempts` (sends made, the first included) and `category` (decision 6) when they apply; unset fields are not written (REQ-SAG-0016). Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601). 5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016). 6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop. 7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. The timeout defaults to 120 s; REQ-SAG-0702 holds the rules. 8. **`send_batch` returns one result per request, each with its input position**, while `on_result` still receives each line as it finishes (REQ-SAG-0702). 11. **sitr is an optional, separate section of the consumer template.** It uses `sc_agent.sitr` only (ADR-SAG-0005, ADR-SAG-0021) and is kept separate from the decision call: extraction runs outside the decision path, and its output feeds the consumer's prompt authoring. In this phase one offline test shows extraction output reaching a dry-run request. 14. **A run is a context object.** `sc_agent.Run(tool=, tool_version=, cache=, ...)` is created once per tool command and closed when its calls are done (`with sc_agent.Run(...) as run:`); creating it mints the run's ULID `run_id` in Rust (as are `session_id` ULIDs), readable as `run.run_id`.”: Last changed 2026-11-24, before ANC-010 (2026-11-26); the sitr and template details were never asked for by the anchor.

ADR-SAG-0021 “**One Logger per process, owned by the entry point.** The entry point is the CLI's `main`, or, for a Python app, its sc-compose generated client. The entry point obtains one sc-observability `Logger`, keeps it for the life of the process and gives it to each Run it creates (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14); the Run passes it to every decision call, flushes it after each call and on exit, and never shuts down a Logger it borrowed. The generated client has no close operation. Library code never builds a Logger of its own while one is injected, and never forwards records to Python `logging`. **The wheel exposes the crate's Logger.** Python may write its own records to it and gives it to the Run of its sc-decidr calls; Rust receives its own Logger object back, so no record crosses a bridge and the process has one queue. **Products.** sc-agent ships three products. sc-observability is a crate linked into each, not a product. | Product | Contains | |---|---| | `decidr` CLI | decidr, sc-observability | | `sitr` CLI | sitr, sc-observability | | sc-decidr wheel | the decidr and sitr Python APIs, sc-observability | There is one Python wheel. A Python process that loads sc-agent has one copy of sc-observability and one Logger, which it injects into decidr and sitr calls alike. Installing the wheel always installs both APIs, whichever one the caller uses. **Defaults.** With no Logger injected, sc-agent uses the default sc-observability Logger, which writes the general log to disk at the paths below. Every decision and sitr call is logged. A caller that wants another general-log sink (a database, nothing) changes the sink of the Logger it injects; that is the caller's responsibility. **Session log.** The session log is always on and is not configurable. sc-agent writes every session row in Rust through its session sink. No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record. A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session. Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink. **Paths.** The log root is `~/.sc-agent`. One function returns a CLI's log root. The CLIs and the wheel call that function; nothing else computes a log path. The wheel's `sc_agent.session_rows(session_ids, *, agent_role, project=None)` is the one reader of the session-log layout: it finds the log root with the same function used to write session rows and returns, as an ok value, a map from each requested `session_id` to its row; a missing id returns `session.not_found` (category `validation`) naming the ids. A generated client reads session rows only through it and has no log-root argument (NFR-SAG-0004). | Entry point | General log | Session logs | |---|---|---| | `decidr` CLI | `logs/decidr.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `sitr` CLI | `logs/sitr.log.jsonl` | none | | `plan-anchor` (generated client) | `logs/plan-anchor.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/plan-anchor/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `judge-jev` (generated client) | `logs/judge-jev.log.jsonl`, holding its decidr and sitr records | `sessions/<repo>/judge-jev/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | A wheel is not an entry point and has no row: it writes to the Logger its caller injects. Every entry point has a row and every cell is filled. The table is updated when an entry point is added. **Session identity.** - `agent_role` is the agent or app making the request. A generated client hardcodes it to its product name; it is not a user setting. - `tool` and `tool_version` name the program that sent the query and its version: the generated client's name, or `decidr` (REQ-SAG-0004). They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14). - `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files). It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set. Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase". **Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms. It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging. A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it. A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.”: Written 2026-11-19, before ANC-005 (2026-11-26) and ANC-020 (2026-11-27).

A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session. Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink. **Paths.** The log root is `~/.sc-agent`. One function returns a CLI's log root. The CLIs and the wheel call that function; nothing else computes a log path. The wheel's `sc_agent.session_rows(session_ids, *, agent_role, project=None)` is the one reader of the session-log layout: it finds the log root with the same function used to write session rows and returns, as an ok value, a map from each requested `session_id` to its row; a missing id returns `session.not_found` (category `validation`) naming the ids. A generated client reads session rows only through it and has no log-root argument (NFR-SAG-0004). | Entry point | General log | Session logs | |---|---|---| | `decidr` CLI | `logs/decidr.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `sitr` CLI | `logs/sitr.log.jsonl` | none | | `plan-anchor` (generated client) | `logs/plan-anchor.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/plan-anchor/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `judge-jev` (generated client) | `logs/judge-jev.log.jsonl`, holding its decidr and sitr records | `sessions/<repo>/judge-jev/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | A wheel is not an entry point and has no row: it writes to the Logger its caller injects. Every entry point has a row and every cell is filled. The table is updated when an entry point is added. **Session identity.** - `agent_role` is the agent or app making the request. A generated client hardcodes it to its product name; it is not a user setting. - `tool` and `tool_version` name the program that sent the query and its version: the generated client's name, or `decidr` (REQ-SAG-0004). They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14). - `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files). It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set. Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase". **Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms. It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging. A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it. A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.”: Written 2026-11-19, before ANC-020 (2026-11-27).

  • `sc-agent` MUST NOT hard-code the network address of any local decision runner.

ADR-SAG-0001 Every decision provider receives one request form

Decision

For decision requests, every decision provider receives the same Jev API request body. `sc-agent` holds one provider table and one model table; the model table is its built-in rows plus the rows configuration adds (REQ-SAG-0102), so a new model works without a release. Decision providers implement one decision trait, and LLM providers one LLM trait (JSON in, JSON out). Jev implements the decision trait over SystemOne. One type per wire format, OpenAI-compatible chat/completions and Anthropic-compatible Messages, implements both traits and is shared by every provider of that format. Before a send, the decision implementation adapts the request to its wire format; the reply is decoded back into a Jev API response. Callers open one `Run` per command (created, used for its calls, then disposed) and use its two methods, `send` for one request and `send_batch` for many; the worker threads, holdoff, cancellation and session logging live behind them.

  • Each decision request MUST specify the required schema through the provider's structured-output feature.
  • If a provider response fails to match the required schema, the decision backend MUST return `decision.schema_mismatch`.
  • The covered model handling the decision request MUST pass the request's inputs to the provider.
  • If the provider rejects a request input, the decision backend MUST return the provider's error.

ADR-SAG-0004 Crate layering and error values

Decision

There are five crates. `sc-agent` is the bottom layer: the provider tables, `send` and `send_batch`, resends, keys, configuration, errors, logging paths and session rows. `sc-treesitter` (tree-sitter extraction) is over `sc-agent`. On top: `decidr` (the decision CLI), `sitr` (the tree-sitter CLI) and `sc-agent-py` (the one wheel, holding the decidr and sitr APIs). CLI agents and SDK agents get their own crates later. Errors are discriminated unions: every call returns `Result<T, E>`, and `E` carries the error info: at least an id and a message. A layer that changes an error keeps the lower error's id and message (REQ-SAG-0002). An error may carry more fields. Whether a crate has its own error type or shares one is not specified.

REQ-SAG-0002 Errors are a discriminated union carried from bottom to top

Statements

  • Every public API MUST return a discriminated union of success and error.
  • Rust APIs MUST return `Result<T, E>` from the lowest layer to the top-level CLI and PyO3 entry points.
  • An error MUST carry the error id and message of every lower-layer error that caused it.
  • A layer that changes an error MUST change it only by adding detail.
  • Error text received from a provider MUST be kept whole.
  • Exception (owner-approved): the API key MUST never appear in an error or log.
  • Every error MUST have a stable id.
  • Rust code MUST NOT panic on any input or runtime failure.
  • A layer MUST NOT drop or replace a lower-layer error id or message.

ADR-SAG-0019 sc-decidr is the one Python decision harness

Decision

The wheel is the one consumer boundary. Decision numbers are stable; there is no decision 3. 1. **The wheel is the consumer boundary.** Every consumer concern except prompt authoring and result interpretation belongs in sc-decidr: model selection, API keys (environment, repo-root `.env`, OS keyring), session logging, the general Logger, errors with a stored category (decisions 2, 5 and 6), limits and cancellation (decisions 7 and 14) and position-tagged batch results (decision 8). Session logging is always on: one row per query whose model call succeeded (a failed call writes no row; its error goes to the general log), at the wheel's default location, tagged with `project` and `agent_role`, written by sc-agent's session sink (ADR-SAG-0021); a cache hit writes no row and one link record (REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0703). All Jev queries and responses therefore take one path. **The integration artifact is a generated module** (REQ-SAG-0018), rendered by each consumer from the sc-compose template `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`; the wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout and `import sc_agent` is unchanged. - The template covers the decision call, model pass-through, logging wiring, cancellation and the error-to-category-to-code mapping. - model selectors are Run arguments. - A result line holds only the generic result fields; session data stays in the session row. The module reads session rows only through `sc_agent.session_rows`, finding a run's queries through its link records or the session_ids in its result lines, and never computes a session-log path. - Python results are typed values, not dicts. - sc-compose is an external render tool, not a wheel dependency; the template's front matter declares its sc-compose minimum (`requires.cli`), declared, not enforced. **The lower-level API stays the contract.** `Run` (with `send` and `send_batch`), `session_rows`, `provider_keys`, `TYPESAFE`, `digest`, `logger`, `log`, `flush` and `sc_agent.sitr` are public, and the generated code uses only them and the standard library. 2. **Typed fields: `attempts` and `category`.** An error value carries at least `id`, `message` and `action`, plus `attempts` (sends made, the first included) and `category` (decision 6) when they apply; unset fields are not written (REQ-SAG-0016). Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601). 5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016). 6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop. 7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. The timeout defaults to 120 s; REQ-SAG-0702 holds the rules. 8. **`send_batch` returns one result per request, each with its input position**, while `on_result` still receives each line as it finishes (REQ-SAG-0702). 11. **sitr is an optional, separate section of the consumer template.** It uses `sc_agent.sitr` only (ADR-SAG-0005, ADR-SAG-0021) and is kept separate from the decision call: extraction runs outside the decision path, and its output feeds the consumer's prompt authoring. In this phase one offline test shows extraction output reaching a dry-run request. 14. **A run is a context object.** `sc_agent.Run(tool=, tool_version=, cache=, ...)` is created once per tool command and closed when its calls are done (`with sc_agent.Run(...) as run:`); creating it mints the run's ULID `run_id` in Rust (as are `session_id` ULIDs), readable as `run.run_id`.

ADR-SAG-0021 One sc-observability Logger per process, owned by the entry point; general logs and session logs in separate trees

Decision

**One Logger per process, owned by the entry point.** The entry point is the CLI's `main`, or, for a Python app, its sc-compose generated client. The entry point obtains one sc-observability `Logger`, keeps it for the life of the process and gives it to each Run it creates (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14); the Run passes it to every decision call, flushes it after each call and on exit, and never shuts down a Logger it borrowed. The generated client has no close operation. Library code never builds a Logger of its own while one is injected, and never forwards records to Python `logging`. **The wheel exposes the crate's Logger.** Python may write its own records to it and gives it to the Run of its sc-decidr calls; Rust receives its own Logger object back, so no record crosses a bridge and the process has one queue. **Products.** sc-agent ships three products. sc-observability is a crate linked into each, not a product. | Product | Contains | |---|---| | `decidr` CLI | decidr, sc-observability | | `sitr` CLI | sitr, sc-observability | | sc-decidr wheel | the decidr and sitr Python APIs, sc-observability | There is one Python wheel. A Python process that loads sc-agent has one copy of sc-observability and one Logger, which it injects into decidr and sitr calls alike. Installing the wheel always installs both APIs, whichever one the caller uses. **Defaults.** With no Logger injected, sc-agent uses the default sc-observability Logger, which writes the general log to disk at the paths below. Every decision and sitr call is logged. A caller that wants another general-log sink (a database, nothing) changes the sink of the Logger it injects; that is the caller's responsibility. **Session log.** The session log is always on and is not configurable. sc-agent writes every session row in Rust through its session sink. No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record. A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session. Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink. **Paths.** The log root is `~/.sc-agent`. One function returns a CLI's log root. The CLIs and the wheel call that function; nothing else computes a log path. The wheel's `sc_agent.session_rows(session_ids, *, agent_role, project=None)` is the one reader of the session-log layout: it finds the log root with the same function used to write session rows and returns, as an ok value, a map from each requested `session_id` to its row; a missing id returns `session.not_found` (category `validation`) naming the ids. A generated client reads session rows only through it and has no log-root argument (NFR-SAG-0004). | Entry point | General log | Session logs | |---|---|---| | `decidr` CLI | `logs/decidr.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `sitr` CLI | `logs/sitr.log.jsonl` | none | | `plan-anchor` (generated client) | `logs/plan-anchor.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/plan-anchor/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `judge-jev` (generated client) | `logs/judge-jev.log.jsonl`, holding its decidr and sitr records | `sessions/<repo>/judge-jev/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | A wheel is not an entry point and has no row: it writes to the Logger its caller injects. Every entry point has a row and every cell is filled. The table is updated when an entry point is added. **Session identity.** - `agent_role` is the agent or app making the request. A generated client hardcodes it to its product name; it is not a user setting. - `tool` and `tool_version` name the program that sent the query and its version: the generated client's name, or `decidr` (REQ-SAG-0004). They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14). - `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files). It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set. Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase". **Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms. It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging. A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it. A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.

REQ-SAG-0003 Log locations and retention

Statements

  • With no Logger injected, each CLI MUST write its general log to `~/.sc-agent/logs/<cli>.log.jsonl`.
  • When `<CLI>_LOG_ROOT` is set and non-empty, that CLI MUST use its value in place of `~/.sc-agent`.
  • When `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` is set and not empty, the generated client MUST use that folder in place of `~/.sc-agent/` for its logs.
  • Session logs MUST be written under `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` (REQ-SAG-0005).
  • A session log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
  • A run log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT contain code that removes a general log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT remove a session log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT remove a run log.

ADR-SAG-0021 restates REQ-SAG-0008
